rows.decision: Authoritative per-actor index of what a like or repost points at. getStratosBacklinks keeps a subject.uri as written when ensureValidAtUri accepts it, and otherwise stores the canonical form subjectLinkTarget builds with parseRecordUri and formatRecordUri. The installed ensureValidAtUri rejects both space spellings, so every space-form subject.uri takes the second path. A string subject is kept only when it is a DID or passes ensureValidAtUri, so a space-form string subject gets no backlink. Both runtime writers use getStratosBacklinks: StratosRecordTransactor behind the sqlite actor store, and PgActorRecordTransactor in the postgres actor store that storage-context.ts builds. The checks that allow one like or repost per subject match linkTo by string equality, and boundary-writes.ts also refuses a batch that names one subject twice by comparing linkTo strings. PgRecordStoreWriter.putRecord has its own getBacklinks, which keeps a subject.uri only when ensureValidAtUri accepts it and so drops every space-form subject; its only constructor is PostgresStorageFactory, which stratos-service/src never instantiates. The key is never rewritten in place, so a like stored under one spelling does not conflict with a like of the same post written in the other.

rows.surface: Feed pagination cursor containing a post URI
rows.decision: Opaque client state of the form {sort_at}::{uri}, taken from the last post of a full page. A malformed cursor and a well-formed stale cursor behave differently. decode splits on the first :: and accepts any two non-empty parts without checking that either is a timestamp or a URI; only a value with no :: or with an empty part decodes to None, and the feed service then serves the first page. A well-formed cursor is forwarded unchanged, and the store applies it as the predicate sort_at < cursor sort_at, or equal sort_at and uri > cursor uri; the uri part is never looked up. A cursor that names a deleted post, or a post URI in the old spelling, therefore keeps filtering: the page continues after its timestamp, and its URI decides by string order only which posts with exactly that timestamp follow. Nothing resets such a cursor to the first page. The feed generator stores no feed cursor, so its database holds nothing to migrate or invalidate for them. A cursor a client holds stays usable after the spelling change; only the tie-break among posts that share its sort_at depends on how the two spellings compare as strings.

rows.decision: authorFromUri and postDeleteTargetFromUri try the core parseRecordUri first and otherwise read the URI as at://{did}/{collection}/{rkey}. authorFromUri strips an at:// prefix and takes the first segment, so a URI the core parser does not accept yields a wrong author, the string at:space for the new spelling. postDeleteTargetFromUri returns null for a URI that does not start with at://, and post-deletion.ts then refuses with 'The post URI is invalid.'. groupIntoThreads attaches a reply to its parent by string equality of reply.parent.uri and the parent's post URI, so a reply whose stored parent URI is spelled differently from the served post shows as a top-level post. Composer.svelte copies the parent's URI into the reply reference and formats the space through the core helpers. All follow the core grammar except the at:// fallbacks.

rows.surface: Space-form reply parent, reply root and embed record URIs in posts
rows.decision: Today a space-form reply.parent.uri is parsed with parseRecordUri in resolveParentBoundaries and its boundary is derived from the space DID and key without reading the parent record; a repo-form parent is looked up in the actor store instead. post-rules.ts isStratosUri accepts a space-form reply.parent.uri, reply.root.uri and embed record.uri when the collection starts with zone.stratos., and isBskyUri reads such a URI with AtUri, which sees the collection as space, so a space-form embed never counts as bsky. These strings are authoritative record content stored inside signed post records: they are never rewritten, so a post stored in the old spelling keeps it, and the parser change must either keep reading that spelling or say how those posts are handled. PostValidator in post-validator.ts is exported from stratos-core but constructed only by ValidatorFactory, which nothing outside stratos-core/tests uses; it reads reply.parent.uri, reply.root.uri and embed record.uri with AtUri, which sees the collection of a legacy space URI as space, so it refuses a space-form reply as CrossNamespaceReply and a space-form embed as CrossNamespaceEmbed, and AtUri throws on at:space/.

rows.decision: space-read/handler.ts maps the requested space to a boundary with spaceUriToBoundary and admits a credential only when its spaceUri equals the requested space string, so a differently spelled equivalent URI is refused; credential-scope.ts and boundary-credential access map the verified credential's spaceUri to a boundary with spaceUriToBoundary; verifiers.ts passes the verified spaceUri through as auth credentials; host-discovery.ts treats the space URI as an opaque lookup key for host overrides. rows.surface: Clubhouse topic route and thread matching on post URIs
rows.decision: A topic is the URI of a feed post, which is a space record URI for a post on a member's own PDS. topicPath throws 'A topic AT URI is required' unless the URI starts with at://, and topicUriFromPath returns null for a topic query value that does not. Today a legacy space-form topic opens and round-trips through the URL; a topic starting at:space/ would make openTopic in App.svelte throw and would be dropped when the URL is read back. RoomFeed.svelte finds the open topic and its thread by string equality of post.uri and reply.root.uri with the topic URI, and builds a reply reference from the served post.uri, so a reply whose stored root.uri keeps the old spelling no longer joins a topic served in the new spelling. App.svelte closes a deleted topic by comparing the topic URI with post.uri, and feed-authors.ts keys profile data by post.uri; both compare strings from the same feed response, so the two sides share one spelling.

rows.surface: Service room-post endpoint reply and delete references
rows.decision: Clubhouse sends a reply's root and parent as the served post URIs, which are space record URIs for posts on a member's own PDS. parseStrongRef accepts a reference only when its uri starts with at:// and contains /zone.stratos.feed.post/. Today a legacy space-form reference passes and is handed unchanged to createRecord through createApprovedRoomPost, where resolveParentBoundaries reads it (see uri-reply-and-embed-strings). A reference starting at:space/ fails parseStrongRef, and the whole request is answered 400 InvalidRoomPost. parseRoomPostDeleteRequest reads the URI with AtUri and requires the collection zone.stratos.feed.post and an rkey; the installed AtUri reads a legacy space URI with the collection space and throws on at:space/, so a space record URI is refused with 400 InvalidRoomPostDelete in either spelling. Room-post deletion serves only Stratos-custody posts, which keep the repo form.

rows.surface: Feedgen feed page reads: URI ordering, cursor comparison and interaction summary joins
rows.decision: list_initial_posts and list_posts_after_cursor join post_boundary to post on uri and order a page by sort_at descending, then uri ascending, so among posts with the same sort_at the order is the byte order of the URI strings. That order differs between at:// and at:space/ URIs, and the cursor comparison uses the same string order (see uri-feed-pagination-cursors). interaction_summaries matches interaction.subject_uri against the served post URIs with IN and returns the counts keyed by subject_uri; ProjectionReader::prepare passes the page's post URIs, and feed_service.rs joins the summaries back by post.uri, so an interaction whose subject_uri is spelled differently from the stored post URI is not counted. blob_post finds a post by exact uri equality for the getBlob uri parameter. All of this is derived projection state.

rows.surface: Rust space host requests, commit verification context and delegation subject
rows.decision: space_host.rs sends the target space URI as the space query parameter of listRepoOps after validate_request checks only that it is non-empty and at most 2048 bytes. pds_space_sync.rs carries target.space_uri unchanged: it looks the cursor up and stages and discards pages by it, keys the per-target lock on it and passes it to commit verification. space_commit.rs commit_context puts the space URI bytes, length-prefixed, into the context that the commit MAC and signature are checked against, so a commit verifies only when the space URI string is byte for byte the one the commit was made over. service_auth.rs mint_space_delegation signs the space URI as the delegation sub claim, and a signed claim is never rewritten. The space URI itself comes from boundary_to_space_uri (see uri-rust-credential-cache and uri-rust-record-uri-callers).

rows.surface: Lexicon fields that carry a space record URI
rows.decision: A post's reply.root and reply.parent and a like's or repost's subject are com.atproto.repo.strongRef, and an embedded record is app.bsky.embed.record; their uri fields declare format at-uri. The installed @atproto/syntax 0.7.4 rejects both space spellings as at-uri: the legacy form has more than two path segments, and the new one lacks at://. A record carrying a space record URI therefore passes lexicon validation on boundary writes only through the validation-copy rewrite (see uri-validation-copy-rewrite), and on the legacy write path StratosValidator discards lexicon errors. The vendored com.atproto and app.bsky files are copies and are never edited. The feed generator's getFeed post uri, its viewer like and repost, and getBlob's uri parameter are plain strings described as AT URI or space record URI, so no format check applies to them. The other Stratos fields declared at-uri (repo write outputs, the space getRecord output, hydrateRecord and hydrateRecords, the zone.stratos.defs subject reference) name Stratos-custody records, which keep the repo form.
